Goal: I can copy a segment and draw a circle with compass and straightedge.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A construction uses only two tools: a straightedge, which draws a line through two points, and a compass, which draws a circle with a given center through a given point. No measuring.

To copy segment AB, open the compass to A and B, then use that opening from a new point. Euclid's first proposition builds an equilateral triangle on AB: draw the circle centered at A through B and the circle centered at B through A. They meet at C. Then AC = AB (radii of one circle) and BC = BA (radii of the other), so all three sides are equal.
